NASB.1: Now after Abimelech died, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel; and he lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
NASB.2: He judged Israel twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried in Shamir.
NASB.3: After him, Jair the Gileadite arose and judged Israel twenty-two years.
NASB.4: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty cities in the land of Gilead that are called Havvoth-jair to this day.
NASB.5: And Jair died and was buried in Kamon.
NASB.6: Then the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD, served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the sons of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines; thus they forsook the LORD and did not serve Him.
NASB.7: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hands of the Philistines and into the hands of the sons of Ammon.
NASB.8: They afflicted and crushed the sons of Israel that year; for eighteen years they [afflicted] all the sons of Israel who were beyond the Jordan in Gilead in the land of the Amorites.
NASB.9: The sons of Ammon crossed the Jordan to fight also against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was greatly distressed.
NASB.10: Then the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, saying, 'We have sinned against You, for indeed, we have forsaken our God and served the Baals.'
NASB.11: The LORD said to the sons of Israel, '[Did I] not [deliver you] from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the sons of Ammon, and the Philistines?
NASB.12: 'Also when the Sidonians, the Amalekites and the Maonites oppressed you, you cried out to Me, and I delivered you from their hands.
NASB.13: 'Yet you have forsaken Me and served other gods; therefore I will no longer deliver you.
NASB.14: 'Go and cry out to the gods which you have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your distress.'
NASB.15: The sons of Israel said to the LORD, 'We have sinned, do to us whatever seems good to You; only please deliver us this day.'
NASB.16: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD; and He could bear the misery of Israel no longer.
NASB.17: Then the sons of Ammon were summoned and they camped in Gilead. And the sons of Israel gathered together and camped in Mizpah.
NASB.18: The people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, 'Who is the man who will begin to fight against the sons of Ammon? He shall become head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.'

ESV.1: After Abimelech there arose to save Israel Tola the son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, and he lived at Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
ESV.2: And he judged Israel twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried at Shamir.
ESV.3: After him arose Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel twenty-two years.
ESV.4: And he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty cities, called Havvoth-jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
ESV.5: And Jair died and was buried in Kamon.
ESV.6: The people of Israel again did what was evil in the sight of the LORD and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, the gods of Syria, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites, and the gods of the Philistines. And they forsook the LORD and did not serve him.
ESV.7: So the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the Ammonites,
ESV.8: and they crushed and oppressed the people of Israel that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the people of Israel who were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
ESV.9: And the Ammonites crossed the Jordan to fight also against Judah and against Benjamin and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was severely distressed.
ESV.10: And the people of Israel cried out to the LORD, saying, “We have sinned against you, because we have forsaken our God and have served the Baals.”
ESV.11: And the LORD said to the people of Israel, “Did I not save you from the Egyptians and from the Amorites, from the Ammonites and from the Philistines?
ESV.12: The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites and the Maonites oppressed you, and you cried out to me, and I saved you out of their hand.
ESV.13: Yet you have forsaken me and served other gods; therefore I will save you no more.
ESV.14: Go and cry out to the gods whom you have chosen; let them save you in the time of your distress.”
ESV.15: And the people of Israel said to the LORD, “We have sinned; do to us whatever seems good to you. Only please deliver us this day.”
ESV.16: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and he became impatient over the misery of Israel.
ESV.17: Then the Ammonites were called to arms, and they encamped in Gilead. And the people of Israel came together, and they encamped at Mizpah.
ESV.18: And the people, the leaders of Gilead, said one to another, “Who is the man who will begin to fight against the Ammonites? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

NKJV.1: After Abimelech there arose to save Israel Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar; and he dwelt in Shamir in the mountains of Ephraim.
NKJV.2: He judged Israel twenty-three years; and he died and was buried in Shamir.
NKJV.3: After him arose Jair, a Gileadite; and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
NKJV.4: Now he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys; they also had thirty towns, which are called “Havoth Jair” to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
NKJV.5: And Jair died and was buried in Camon.
NKJV.6: Then the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD, and served the Baals and the Ashtoreths, the gods of Syria, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the people of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines; and they forsook the LORD and did not serve Him.
NKJV.7: So the anger of the LORD was hot against Israel; and He sold them into the hands of the Philistines and into the hands of the people of Ammon.
NKJV.8: From that year they harassed and oppressed the children of Israel for eighteen years—all the children of Israel who were on the other side of the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, in Gilead.
NKJV.9: Moreover the people of Ammon crossed over the Jordan to fight against Judah also, against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was severely distressed.

NKJV.11: So the LORD said to the children of Israel, “Did I not deliver you from the Egyptians and from the Amorites and from the people of Ammon and from the Philistines?

NKJV.13: Yet you have forsaken Me and served other gods. Therefore I will deliver you no more.
NKJV.14: “Go and cry out to the gods which you have chosen; let them deliver you in your time of distress.”

NKJV.16: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD. And His soul could no longer endure the misery of Israel.

NKJV.18: And the people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, “Who is the man who will begin the fight against the people of Ammon? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

NLT.1: After Abimelech died, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, was the next person to rescue Israel. He was from the tribe of Issachar but lived in the town of Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
NLT.2: He judged Israel for twenty-three years. When he died, he was buried in Shamir.
NLT.3: After Tola died, Jair from Gilead judged Israel for twenty-two years.
NLT.4: His thirty sons rode around on thirty donkeys, and they owned thirty towns in the land of Gilead, which are still called the Towns of Jair.
NLT.5: When Jair died, he was buried in Kamon.
NLT.6: Again the Israelites did evil in the LORD’s sight. They served the images of Baal and Ashtoreth, and the gods of Aram, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia. They abandoned the LORD and no longer served him at all.
NLT.7: So the LORD burned with anger against Israel, and he turned them over to the Philistines and the Ammonites,
NLT.8: who began to oppress them that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites east of the Jordan River in the land of the Amorites (that is, in Gilead).
NLT.9: The Ammonites also crossed to the west side of the Jordan and attacked Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. The Israelites were in great distress.
NLT.10: Finally, they cried out to the LORD for help, saying, “We have sinned against you because we have abandoned you as our God and have served the images of Baal.”
NLT.11: The LORD replied, “Did I not rescue you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines,
NLT.12: the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites? When they oppressed you, you cried out to me for help, and I rescued you.
NLT.13: Yet you have abandoned me and served other gods. So I will not rescue you anymore.
NLT.14: Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen! Let them rescue you in your hour of distress!”
NLT.15: But the Israelites pleaded with the LORD and said, “We have sinned. Punish us as you see fit, only rescue us today from our enemies.”
NLT.16: Then the Israelites put aside their foreign gods and served the LORD. And he was grieved by their misery.
NLT.17: At that time the armies of Ammon had gathered for war and were camped in Gilead, and the people of Israel assembled and camped at Mizpah.
NLT.18: The leaders of Gilead said to each other, “Whoever attacks the Ammonites first will become ruler over all the people of Gilead.”

CSB17.1: After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo became judge and began to deliver Israel. He was from Issachar and lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
CSB17.2: Tola judged Israel twenty-three years and when he died, was buried in Shamir.
CSB17.3: After him came Jair the Gileadite, <sup>ⓜ</sup> who judged Israel twenty-two years.
CSB17.4: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys. They had thirty towns <sup>[1]</sup> in Gilead, which are still called Jair’s Villages <sup>[2]</sup> today.
CSB17.5: When Jair died, he was buried in Kamon.
CSB17.6: Then the Israelites again did what was evil in the sight of the LORD. <sup>ⓝ</sup> They worshiped the Baals and the Ashtoreths, the gods of Aram, Sidon, and Moab, and the gods of the Ammonites and the Philistines. <sup>ⓐ</sup> They abandoned the LORD and did not worship him. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.7: So the LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them to <sup>[3]</sup> the Philistines and the Ammonites. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.8: They shattered and crushed the Israelites that year, and for eighteen years they did the same to all the Israelites who were on the other side of the Jordan <sup>ⓓ</sup> in the land of the Amorites <sup>ⓔ</sup> in Gilead.
CSB17.9: The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim. Israel was greatly oppressed,
CSB17.10: so they cried out to the LORD, saying, “We have sinned against you. <sup>ⓕ</sup> We have abandoned our God and worshiped the Baals.”
CSB17.11: The LORD said to the Israelites, “When the Egyptians, <sup>ⓖ</sup> Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines,
CSB17.12: Sidonians, Amalekites, and Maonites <sup>[4]</sup> <sup>ⓗ</sup> oppressed you, and you cried out to me, did I not deliver you from them?
CSB17.13: But you have abandoned me and worshiped other gods. Therefore, I will not deliver you again.
CSB17.14: Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. <sup>ⓘ</sup> Let them deliver you whenever you are oppressed.”
CSB17.15: But the Israelites said, “We have sinned. Deal with us as you see fit; <sup>[5]</sup> only rescue us <sup>ⓙ</sup> today!”
CSB17.16: So they got rid of the foreign gods <sup>ⓚ</sup> among them and worshiped the LORD, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and he became weary <sup>ⓜ</sup> of Israel’s misery.
CSB17.17: The Ammonites were called together, and they camped in Gilead. So the Israelites assembled and camped at Mizpah. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.18: The rulers <sup>[6]</sup> of Gilead said to one another, “Which man will begin the fight against the Ammonites? He will be the leader of all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

WEB.1: After Abimelech, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.

WEB.3: After him Jair, the Gileadite arose, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
WEB.4: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts, and they had thirty cities, which are called Havvoth Jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
WEB.5: Jair died, and was buried in Kamon.

WEB.18: The people, the princes of Gilead, said to one another, “Who is the man who will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

AMP.1: After Abimelech died, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel; and he lived in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim.
AMP.2: Tola judged Israel for twenty-three years; then he died and was buried in Shamir.
AMP.3: After him, Jair the Gileadite arose, and he judged Israel for twenty-two years.
AMP.4: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns in the land of Gilead that are called Havvoth-jair (towns of Jair) to this day.
AMP.5: And Jair died and was buried in Kamon.
AMP.6: Then the Israelites again did what was evil in the sight of the LORD; they served the Baals, the Ashtaroth (female deities), the gods of Aram (Syria), the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned the LORD and did not serve Him.
AMP.7: So the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and He sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the Ammonites,
AMP.8: and they oppressed and crushed Israel that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites who were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
AMP.9: The Ammonites crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was greatly distressed.
AMP.10: Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD [for help], saying, "We have sinned against You, because we have abandoned (rejected) our God and have served the Baals."
AMP.11: The LORD said to the Israelites, "Did I not rescue you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines?
AMP.12: Also when the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites oppressed and crushed you, you cried out to Me, and I rescued you from their hands.
AMP.13: Yet you have abandoned (rejected) Me and served other gods; therefore I will no longer rescue you.
AMP.14: Go, cry out to the gods you have chosen; let them rescue you in your time of distress."
AMP.15: The Israelites said to the LORD, "We have sinned, do to us whatever seems good to You; only please rescue us this day."
AMP.16: So they removed the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD; and He could bear the misery of Israel no longer.
AMP.17: Then the Ammonites were assembled together and they camped in Gilead. And the sons of Israel assembled and camped at Mizpah.
AMP.18: The people, the leaders of Gilead (Israel) said to one another, "Who is the man who will begin to fight against the Ammonites? He shall become head over all the inhabitants of Gilead."

NET.1: After Abimelech’s death, Tola son of Puah, grandson of Dodo, from the tribe of Issachar, rose up to deliver Israel. He lived in Shamir in the Ephraimite hill country.
NET.2: He led Israel for twenty-three years, then died and was buried in Shamir.
NET.3: Jair the Gileadite rose up after him; he led Israel for twenty-two years.
NET.4: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys and possessed thirty cities. To this day these towns are called Havvoth Jair — they are in the land of Gilead.
NET.5: Jair died and was buried in Kamon.
NET.6: The Israelites again did evil in the LORD’s sight. They worshiped the Baals and the Ashtars, as well as the gods of Syria, Sidon, Moab, the Ammonites, and the Philistines. They abandoned the LORD and did not worship him.
NET.7: The LORD was furious with Israel and turned them over to the Philistines and Ammonites.
NET.8: They ruthlessly oppressed the Israelites that eighteenth year — that is, all the Israelites living east of the Jordan in Amorite country in Gilead.
NET.9: The Ammonites crossed the Jordan to fight with Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Israel suffered greatly.
NET.10: The Israelites cried out for help to the LORD: “We have sinned against you. We abandoned our God and worshiped the Baals.”
NET.11: The LORD said to the Israelites, “Did I not deliver you from Egypt, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines,
NET.12: the Sidonians, Amalek, and Midian when they oppressed you? You cried out for help to me, and I delivered you from their power.
NET.13: But since you abandoned me and worshiped other gods, I will not deliver you again.
NET.14: Go and cry for help to the gods you have chosen! Let them deliver you from trouble!”
NET.15: But the Israelites said to the LORD, “We have sinned. You do to us as you see fit, but deliver us today!”
NET.16: They threw away the foreign gods they owned and worshiped the LORD. Finally the LORD grew tired of seeing Israel suffer so much.
NET.17: The Ammonites assembled and camped in Gilead; the Israelites gathered together and camped in Mizpah.
NET.18: The leaders of Gilead said to one another, “Who is willing to lead the charge against the Ammonites? He will become the leader of all who live in Gilead!”

NRSVCE.1: After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, who lived at Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim, rose to deliver Israel.
NRSVCE.2: He judged Israel twenty-three years. Then he died, and was buried at Shamir.
NRSVCE.3: After him came Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel twenty-two years.
NRSVCE.4: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys; and they had thirty towns, which are in the land of Gilead, and are called Havvoth-jair to this day.
NRSVCE.5: Jair died, and was buried in Kamon.
NRSVCE.6: The Israelites again did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, worshiping the Baals and the Astartes, the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites, and the gods of the Philistines. Thus they abandoned the LORD, and did not worship him.
NRSVCE.7: So the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the Ammonites,
NRSVCE.8: and they crushed and oppressed the Israelites that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites that were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
NRSVCE.9: The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah and against Benjamin and against the house of Ephraim; so that Israel was greatly distressed.
NRSVCE.10: So the Israelites cried to the LORD, saying, “We have sinned against you, because we have abandoned our God and have worshiped the Baals.”
NRSVCE.11: And the LORD said to the Israelites, “Did I not deliver you from the Egyptians and from the Amorites, from the Ammonites and from the Philistines?
NRSVCE.12: The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites, oppressed you; and you cried to me, and I delivered you out of their hand.
NRSVCE.13: Yet you have abandoned me and worshiped other gods; therefore I will deliver you no more.
NRSVCE.14: Go and cry to the gods whom you have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your distress.”
NRSVCE.15: And the Israelites said to the LORD, “We have sinned; do to us whatever seems good to you; but deliver us this day!”
NRSVCE.16: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and worshiped the LORD; and he could no longer bear to see Israel suffer.
NRSVCE.17: Then the Ammonites were called to arms, and they encamped in Gilead; and the Israelites came together, and they encamped at Mizpah.
NRSVCE.18: The commanders of the people of Gilead said to one another, “Who will begin the fight against the Ammonites? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

NIV.1:
Tola
After the time of Abimelech a man of Issachar, Tola son of Puah, the son of Dodo, rose to save Israel. He lived in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim.
NIV.2: He led Israel twenty-three years; then he died, and was buried in Shamir.
NIV.3:
Jair
He was followed by Jair of Gilead, who led Israel twenty-two years.
NIV.4: He had thirty sons, who rode thirty donkeys. They controlled thirty towns in Gilead, which to this day are called Havvoth Jair.
NIV.5: When Jair died, he was buried in Kamon.
NIV.6:
Jephthah
Again the Israelites did evil in the eyes of the Lord. They served the Baals and the Ashtoreths, and the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites and the gods of the Philistines. And because the Israelites forsook the Lord and no longer served him,
NIV.7: he became angry with them. He sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the Ammonites,
NIV.8: who that year shattered and crushed them. For eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites on the east side of the Jordan in Gilead, the land of the Amorites.
NIV.9: The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin and the house of Ephraim; and Israel was in great distress.
NIV.10: Then the Israelites cried out to the Lord, “We have sinned against you, forsaking our God and serving the Baals.”
NIV.11: The Lord replied, “When the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines,
NIV.12: the Sidonians, the Amalekites and the Maonites oppressed you and you cried to me for help, did I not save you from their hands?
NIV.13: But you have forsaken me and served other gods, so I will no longer save you.
NIV.14: Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them save you when you are in trouble!”
NIV.15: But the Israelites said to the Lord, “We have sinned. Do with us whatever you think best, but please rescue us now.”
NIV.16: Then they got rid of the foreign gods among them and served the Lord. And he could bear Israel’s misery no longer.
NIV.17: When the Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead, the Israelites assembled and camped at Mizpah.
NIV.18: The leaders of the people of Gilead said to each other, “Whoever will launch the attack against the Ammonites will be the head of all those living in Gilead.”

MSG.1: Tola son of Puah, the son of Dodo, was next after Abimelech. He rose to the occasion to save Israel. He was a man of Issachar. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
MSG.2: He judged Israel for twenty-three years and then died and was buried at Shamir.
MSG.3: After him, Jair the Gileadite stepped into leadership. He judged Israel for twenty-two years.
MSG.4: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys and had thirty towns in Gilead. The towns are still called Jair's Villages.
MSG.5: Jair died and was buried in Kamon.
MSG.6: And then the People of Israel went back to doing evil in God's sight. They worshiped the Baal gods and Ashtoreth goddesses: gods of Aram, Sidon, and Moab; gods of the Ammonites and the Philistines. They just walked off and left God, quit worshiping him.
MSG.7: And God exploded in hot anger at Israel and sold them off to the Philistines and Ammonites, who,
MSG.8: beginning that year, bullied and battered the People of Israel mercilessly. For eighteen years they had them under their thumb, all the People of Israel who lived east of the Jordan in the Amorite country of Gilead.
MSG.9: Then the Ammonites crossed the Jordan to go to war also against Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Israel was in a bad way!
MSG.10: The People of Israel cried out to God for help: "We've sinned against you! We left our God and worshiped the Baal gods!"
MSG.11: God answered the People of Israel: "When the Egyptians, Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines, Sidonians
MSG.12: —even Amalek and Midian!—oppressed you and you cried out to me for help, I saved you from them.
MSG.13: And now you've gone off and betrayed me, worshiping other gods. I'm not saving you anymore.
MSG.14: Go ahead! Cry out for help to the gods you've chosen—let them get you out of the mess you're in!"
MSG.15: The People of Israel said to God: "We've sinned. Do to us whatever you think best, but please, get us out of this!"
MSG.16: Then they cleaned house of the foreign gods and worshiped only God. And God took Israel's troubles to heart.
MSG.17: The Ammonites prepared for war, setting camp in Gilead. The People of Israel set their rival camp in Mizpah.
MSG.18: The leaders in Gilead said, "Who will stand up for us against the Ammonites? We'll make him head over everyone in Gilead!"
